payload.title: NVDA: the next confirmed daily cycle low, then a higher daily low or a bullish daily trend-line break
payload.context: The 12 Nov daily cycle low failed on 18 Nov. I want the next daily cycle low confirmed first, then a higher daily low or a bullish daily trend-line break as a sign the decline is over. If the weekly cycle low breaks, the idea needs a rethink.
payload.nextStep: When step 2 fires, look at the NVDA daily and weekly charts and decide whether to act.

conditions.label: Next confirmed daily cycle low after 12 Nov (any price)

invalidation.label: The latest confirmed weekly cycle low breaks

explanation:
Here's what I'll set up for NVDA. It's a DWLF 'thesis': a saved note of what you're waiting for, which DWLF checks for you every night.

What I'll save:
- Step 1: the next confirmed daily cycle low dated after 12 Nov, at any price.
- Step 2: DWLF only starts checking this once step 1 is met. It's met by whichever comes first: a higher daily cycle low (a later confirmed daily low above the step-1 low), or a bullish break of a daily trend line.
- Challenged if: NVDA closes below its latest confirmed weekly cycle low. I've used DWLF's own 'weekly low breaks' event because the new daily low doesn't exist yet, so there's no price to set a level against. If you'd rather use a specific weekly price you already have in mind, give me the number and I'll use a weekly close below it instead.
- Your reasons and your next step are saved with it, and they're repeated in every alert.

Before saving for real, I'll do a dry run. That restates each condition in plain words and confirms it can still happen. I'll show you that restatement and only save once you say it's right. If something is already true right now, DWLF refuses the save. For example, a daily low after 12 Nov may already be confirmed. If that happens I'll tell you, and you can choose whether to save it anyway.

What DWLF does for you:
- You decide once, and you don't have to re-check the chart every day. DWLF checks each condition once a night after the close.
- It tells you when a step is met or the thesis is challenged. That comes as an in-app notification, and as a Telegram digest if you've set Telegram up. I can also read the same events for you.
- Honest timing. Each event shows when DWLF could first have known it; a cycle low, for example, is only confirmed a few bars after its low bar. Nothing that happened before you saved counts. Step 2 also can't be met by something confirmed on the same bar as step 1's low.
- It checks exactly the conditions above, using DWLF's own cycle and trend-line data, not someone's reading of the chart.
- 'How close' view: for each pending condition it can show, for example, how developed a forming daily low is. It also keeps a journal: edits are saved as new versions, and you can see the history on the Theses page (Log -> Theses).

What it doesn't do:
- It's not intraday. You'll hear about events after that day's close, not when they happen.
- It's not advice. It reports what the market did against your conditions. It doesn't tell you to buy or sell, it doesn't forecast, and it doesn't place trades.
- The trend-line condition counts any active daily trend line that breaks upward. You can't pick one particular line.
- If the weekly low breaks, the thesis doesn't close on its own. It's marked 'challenged' and waits for you to choose: keep it, revise it, or close it with a note on what you did. I'll record your choice; I won't make it for you.
- It only checks the condition types DWLF can detect. Anything else, such as news or earnings, would have to be a manual condition that you tick off yourself.
- Depending on your plan, exact prices and distances to levels may be hidden. The % change since you saved is always shown.
